doc.title: Alcide "Slow Drag" Pavageau and Lawrence Marrero Interview, 1957-09-01

title: Lumber yard and furniture store jobs
summary: Marrero describes working at a furniture store and a lumber yard on the Industrial Canal before George called him back, and says he has not touched his banjo for a long time.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Yeah, I didn't know. I thought you were working in the furniture. No, not that time, no.
Oh, I didn't know. No, out of the lumber yard. Then I left the furniture store, then out of the lumber yard. And I was working hard, too. I was so glad with George come back and met that job.
Where was that? Where was the lumber yard?

That's where down on Galois, and you remember about a Pippa mill down there? Around Flintcote? Yeah, about Flintcote, right across Flintcote. You ought to know where Flintcote is. I don't know if you knew where it was at. That's where down Galois, at the Duster Canal. Oh, yeah. The Duster Canal.
Oh, yeah. The Duster Canal. The Duster Canal. The Duster Canal, mostly, yeah. That's where I was working at, Dudley Lumbia Company. You
